minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 27, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:04 p.m., on October 27, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 22, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:20 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One Matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 (one case.)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Schlicht recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  October 27, 2015
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered a matter of present litigation in
Closed Session. The City Council gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Mark O’Meara as a Hometown Hero

  Council Member Sachs and Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Mark
  O'Meara. Paul Bucknum and Bob Breton, on behalf of the Heritage Committee, presented
  Mr. O'Meara with a copy of the Mission Viejo history book.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of appreciation to Mary Ann Harcharik for volunteer
  hours at the library and Beverly Catte, Sandra Reis, and Kathy Sandals for volunteer hours
  at the Animal Services Center. Volunteers Sue Goldberger, Joleen Failor, Leitha Duvinage,
  and Suzanne Hodgin were unable to attend the meeting.

P3.  Presentation on the Yellow Fever Mosquito

  The City Council received the presentation from Orange County Mosquito and Vector
  Control District Trustee, Dave Leckness, and Director of Communications, Jared Dever.

P4.  Mission Viejo’s Sponsorship Program

  The City Council received the presentation from Mark Nix, Director of Recreation and
  Community Services.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: announced that there will be a free flu shot clinic on Thursday, November
5, 2015, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Murray Community and Senior Center. She stated
that she hopes to include a drive-by service but she needs two more nurses to do that and anyone
interested can contact her at 470-3062.

Carole Weidler, M.V.: announced that seventeen high school marching bands are coming to
participate in the Western Band Invitational competition at Mission Viejo High School on

City Council Minutes  2  October 27, 2015
 Saturday, October 31 beginning at noon. She stated that it is a great way for residents to spend the
afternoon and the event also supports local high schools  .

Jason Harnett, M.V.: discussed the players and the events that are planned for the Uniqlo
Wheelchair Doubles Masters which will be held November 3-7, 2015, at the Marguerite Tennis
Pavilion.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 4 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 13, 2015, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated October 2, 2015 in the Amount of $679,939.23

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Requests by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and the Mission Viejo Friends of
  the Arts Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage
  Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

  Approved the requests by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and the Mission Viejo
  Friends of the Arts Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage
  Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

City Council Minutes  3  October 27, 2015
 6.  Maintenance of Traffic Signals, Appurtenance, Interconnect, Flashing Beacons,
  Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights, and CCTV Cameras-Contract Change
  Order 3

  (1) Approved Contract Change Order 3 to Contract A12-01 with Siemens Industry, Inc., in
  the amount of $80,382.23, comprised of $25,382.23 for purchase order 150014 and
  $55,000 for purchase order 21600064; and (2) adopted Resolution 15-50 Amending the
  Fiscal Year 2015-2016 Operating Budget for Costs Related to Traffic Signal Maintenance.

7.  Orange County Transportation Authority 2015-2016 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  (1) Adopted Resolution 15-51 Approving the Submittal of the Intersection Capacity
  Enhancement Projects under the Regional Capacity Program (Project O) to the Orange
  County Transportation Authority for Funding under the Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program; and (2) adopt Resolution 15-52 Approving the Submittal of the El Toro
  Road Corridor, Marguerite Parkway Corridor, and Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Corridor
  Improvement Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding Under
  the Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program
  (Project P).

8.  Request for Removal of Existing Parking Restrictions on Bellogente

  Adopted Resolution 15-53 Approving the Removal of Existing "No Parking 7:00 a.m. to
  8:00 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, September Through June"
  Restrictions on Both Sides of Bellogente South of Crown Valley Parkway.

9.  Destruction of Records – Citywide Annual Records Purge

  Adopted Resolution 15-54 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain
  City Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of California.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register Dated October 9, 2015 in the Amount of $2,234,760.77

  Mayor Schlicht asked about a $5,000 payment to Land CM Corp. She expressed concern
  with cronyism stating that the company is owned by a former City employee. She also
  noted that there seem to be miscellaneous piecemeal plant purchases and she stated that the
  city's slopes are in horrendous condition. She further expressed concern that there is no
  slope rehabilitation plan in place.

City Council Minutes  4  October 27, 2015
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the plants
  on the check register are for a particular projects and that there is, in fact, a slope
  maintenance plan in place. He noted that staff is paying special attention to drought issues
  as was directed by the City Council.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

10.  Amendment to FY 15/16 Budget Due to Carryover of Certain Revenue and
  Expenditure Accounts and Appropriated Reserves

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 15-55 Amending The FY 2015/16 City Budget and allocating $1.1
  million for the refurbishment of the Marguerite Aquatics Complex with the balance of
  $300,000 going into the economic development fund.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

11.  Street Sweeping Contract rate increase consideration for the Sunset Property
  Services Street Sweeping Contract

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to reject the request
  and authorize City staff to issue a change order to the contract for the new rate increase
  starting July 1, 2015, and continue on until the end of the contract term and issue a one
  time "catch up" payment of $2,700.

City Council Minutes  5  October 27, 2015
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to call
  the question and end discussion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Raths and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

12.  Wireless Internet Services for The Village Shopping Center (Center)

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report and stated that it is the City's preference that
  Cox Communications provide internet service to the shopping center however, staff has
  come up with a plan should Cox decide to not provide the service.

  Bob Ollry, M.V.: expressed concern with the proposal to offer internet service to the
  Village Shopping Center.

  Milad Khatami, M.V., stated that his company TelePacific Communications can provide
  internet service to the tenants of the shopping center.

  The following business owners spoke in favor of the City's proposal for the City to provide
  internet access: Bob Stewart, M.V.; Mary Kim, M.V.; Dan Ho, Aliso Viejo; Wade
  Weiman, Rolling Hills Estates; Holly Joslin, representing the Edwald Family Trust,
  Laguna Niguel.

  Charlie Kinstler, owner of Saddleback Lanes, submitted a written comment in favor of the
  City providing internet access to the shopping center.

  The following presented written and/or email comments in opposition to the proposal for
  the City to provide internet access: Al Holguin, M.V.; Larry Gilbert, M.V.; and Desi Kiss,
  M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to direct staff
  to return to the City Council on December 8, 2015, with a report on how the matter will be
  solved between the businesses and private entities.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  October 27, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:33 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:44
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented a brief report.

14.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

15.  OCTA Director’s Report; Recommendation of OCTA Director for District 5;
  Direction to City Selection Committee Representative

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht confirmed that she will be attending the City Selection
  Committee meeting. She stated that this has never been on an agenda before and she
  feels that the Council is trying to dilute her authority as Mayor.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to direct
  that the City of Mission Viejo's vote for OCTA Board Member, 5th District, will be for
  Frank Ury.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to call the question
  and end the discussion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  October 27, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

16.  City Attorney Report on Medical Marijuana Regulation and Safety Act

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to direct staff to
  draft the necessary ordinance to ban medical marijuana cultivation, transportation,
  distribution, and dispensaries in Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Report on Completion of Case No. 15-210897 (Loss of Single Page Document
  Submitted at the 9/8/15 City Council Meeting

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report and stated that the investigation garnered no
  particular findings and is now closed.

18.  Landscape Maintenance Contract Area #1 - Termination and Re-Bidding

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to table this matter
  to the next meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

City Council Minutes  8  October 27, 2015
 19.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum discussed her participation in recent events including the Tee it Up
Fore Marines golf tournament, the annual Walk Against Drugs and Disaster Preparedness Fair,
Senator Pat Bates’ open house, and Hometown Halloween. She also announced upcoming events
including La Paz Intermediate School’s Zombie Madness on October 30, a booster fundraiser and
band competition at Mission Viejo High School on October 31, and the Wheelchair Tennis Masters
from November 3-7 at the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he had a great time playing in the Tee it Up Fore Marines
golf tournament. He noted that the Mission Viejo Country Club members who played in the
tournament and donated to the charity gave as much as $10,000 and he expressed pride in their
generosity.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury reminded residents that there are a lot of repairs going on around the City in
preparation for the El Nino storms. He also thanked his colleagues for their support for his
reappointment to the OCTA Board of Directors.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths said as a former Marine, it was great to participate in the Tee it Up Fore
Marines golf tournament. He thanked staff and the Marine Adoption Committee for putting the
event together and everything they do to help the Headquarter Battalion 1st Marine Division at
Camp Pendleton. He stated that the Walk Against drugs was a great success and he enjoyed the
“shake it up” exhibits which demonstrated what to do in an earthquake. Mayor Pro Tem Raths
offered a reminder that the Uniqlo wheelchair tennis tournament is coming up and he encouraged
residents to participate in that event. He also offered condolences to his friends, the Corless family
on the loss of their father, Major Joe Corless, U.S. Army, retired. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Raths
announced that during the break, he received a text from the Orange County Register reporter who
wrote a story on the City’s proposal to offer wireless internet service to the shopping center across
from city hall. The reporter sad that 10 days ago, when the article was published, the City hadn’t
finalized its cost recovery plan but any future stories will include that information.

City Council Minutes  9  October 27, 2015
 Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht announced that she will submit, for the public record, a complaint letter from
resident A. Gora regarding concerns in his neighborhood. She reminded residents that the yellow
fever mosquito has been found in Mission Viejo. What makes them different, besides the potential
to carry disease, is that they thrive both indoors and outdoors and bite during the day. She
encouraged residents to call Vector Control if they see the mosquitos or are getting bitten during
the day. Mayor Schlicht discussed her attendance at the Vocational Visions barbecue and she noted
that that organization does marvelous work as they enhance our community by developing the
talents of both adults and minors who have intellectual developmental disabilities. She also said
she had a good conversation with Senator Pat Bates and Congresswoman Mimi Walters on the
problem with PACE loans and she will submit, for the public record, a briefing on how PACE
financing impacts realtors who continue to express concerns on behalf of homeowners. Mayor
Schlicht discussed her attendance at the Walk Against Drugs with keynote speaker Curtis Beach,
her city hall tour with Cub Scout Pack 603, and the South Orange County Association of Mayors
breakfast with an informative presentation by Ron Kingston, a leader in PACE loan reform. Mayor
Schlicht stated that she doesn’t submit to all the power struggles that come with the trappings of
public of office but instead she does her best to try to do what’s right for the voters. She said that
reasonable minds can disagree and there is no reason to be spiteful. Mayor Schlicht stated that it
isn’t the job of government to compete with the private sector and she is glad that the Council is
holding Cox Communications accountable on the internet access at the Village Shopping
Center. In conclusion, she shared a quote from Mark VanDoren: “An unexamined idea, to
paraphrase Socrates, is not worth having and a society whose ideas are never explored for possible
error may eventually find its foundations insecure.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:46 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 10, 2015

City Council Minutes  10  October 27, 2015
